sentences.text: The genus is known from two partial skull bones, including a holotype premaxilla measuring approximately 201 mm in length, 115 mm in preserved width, and 103 mm in height.
The genus name Oxalaia honors the African deity Oxalá, while the species name quilombensis refers to quilombo settlements founded by escaped slaves.
Fossils were discovered in 1999 on Cajual Island within the Alcântara Formation at the Laje do Coringa locality.
Alexander Kellner and colleagues formally described the species Oxalaia quilombensis in 2011.
Tall neural spines on its tail vertebrae may have aided in swimming, and its skull and dentition indicate a partly piscivorous lifestyle similar to modern crocodilians.
Oxalaia is classified within the superfamily Megalosauroidea, with a fossil range spanning the Upper Cretaceous.

It is assigned to the subfamily Spinosaurinae due to its upper jaw morphology and lack of fine tooth serrations typical of baryonychines, distinguished by features like sculptured palatal premaxillae and two replacement teeth per position.
This animal lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Northeast Region of Brazil between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
It inhabited a humid tropical forest habitat during the Late Cretaceous, a time when its relatives Suchomimus and Cristatusaurus also existed.
It is debated whether Oxalaia is a junior synonym of Spinosaurus or a distinct genus, and whether Oxalaia quilombensis is a distinct species or a modern synonym of the African genus Spinosaurus.

In 2020, Smyth and colleagues argued that the distinguishing features were insufficient for a separate taxon and resulted from individual variation, while it remains impossible to confirm if the smaller number of teeth is due to ontogeny without a larger sample size.
